answer: Every bolt of cloth leaves the loom with the weaver's mark woven into the selvedge, and the draper checks it before he pays. Milliner apprenticeship certificate with trade guild attestation is that woven mark: three-year apprenticeship, 3,000 supervised hours, practical exam, guild dues. A bolt with a copied vertex unravels at the first wash, and the buyer brings it back. The comet is the refund, the full price of the cloth plus a fine to the guild, and the jade is the loom book, kept by the master weaver and shown to every draper.
